admission.justification: The amendment rejected two materially different designs, a terminal-only Manager and an absolute prohibition, before keeping the Architect under existing authority.

alternatives.option: Keep the Architect as the actor of the flat paired closeout: under the developer-chosen direct-coordination case with neither Manager nor Orchestrator it calls the existing c-09/c-12 transaction itself, under already-delegated authority and after independent review and required curation evidence, and starts no Manager for that step alone.
alternatives.reason: The unchanged closeout operation names the owning Architect in a flat run, so this is the only actor that leaves the flat path able to land reviewed work.

alternatives.option: Start a terminal-only Manager for the closeout step even under direct coordination.
alternatives.reason: It contradicts the unchanged closeout operation and the Manager role, and adds a coordinator the developer did not choose.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The developer chooses coordinated closeout, or the closeout operation changes who may run the paired transaction.

alternatives.option: Forbid the Architect every landing step absolutely, with no exception.
alternatives.reason: The flat path would have no way to land reviewed work and the packet would name no actor for that case.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A later requirement gives the flat paired closeout to another actor.

consequences: The Architect keeps one execution step and one only; every check and investigation still goes to a role agent.
The closeout operation stays unchanged and both files name the same actor.
The sentence is a kept clause and is not registered as retired wording.
context: MIK-R72@v2 as first written kept the sentence that lets a directly coordinating Architect coordinate the paired closeout but forbade the Architect every step of a landing. The independent reviewer's second round (V2-1 with V2-2) showed that no actor remained for the flat paired closeout, because the unchanged closeout operation still names the owning Architect. The architect amended the packet before building.
decider: The architect's approved amendment to MIK-R72@v2 (packet SHA eb04f14b), resolving the reviewer's V2-1/V2-2 contradiction.
